questions.q: For a particle in a one-dimensional box of length L, if L is doubled the ground-state energy becomes:
The Heisenberg uncertainty principle for position and momentum states:
questions.e: The product of the standard deviations is bounded below by ħ/2.

questions.q: Ignoring spin, how many orbitals (degenerate states) are there in the n = 2 level of the hydrogen atom?
questions.e: Degeneracy is n²: one 2s and three 2p orbitals.

questions.q: Why does a particle in a box have a nonzero minimum (zero-point) energy?
questions.m: Confining the particle to length L fixes Δx ~ L, so the uncertainty principle requires Δp ≳ ħ/L and thus a nonzero kinetic energy. Equivalently, the wavefunction must vanish at the walls, so n = 0 would give ψ = 0 everywhere; the lowest allowed solution (n = 1) has curvature and hence energy h²/8mL².

questions.q: One mole of ideal gas expands reversibly and isothermally from V to 2V at temperature T. The work done on the gas is:
questions.e: w = −nRT ln(V₂/V₁) = −RT ln 2 (the gas does work on surroundings).

questions.q: For an ideal gas, C_P,m − C_V,m equals:
questions.e: From H = U + nRT: C_P − C_V = nR for an ideal gas.

questions.q: The entropy change of an ideal gas in free expansion into vacuum from V₁ to V₂ at constant T is nR ln(V₂/V₁) even though q = 0. Explain.
questions.m: Entropy is a state function; ΔS must be computed along a reversible path between the same endpoints, e.g. reversible isothermal expansion, where q_rev = nRT ln(V₂/V₁) and ΔS = q_rev/T = nR ln(V₂/V₁). The actual irreversible process has q = 0, so ΔS_surr = 0 and ΔS_total = ΔS_system > 0, consistent with the second law.

questions.q: At constant T and P, a process is spontaneous when:
questions.e: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS < 0 is the criterion for spontaneity at constant T and P.

questions.q: At 298 K, ΔG° = −5.7 kJ/mol. The equilibrium constant is approximately:
For a closed system doing only PV work, (∂G/∂P)_T equals:
questions.e: dG = V dP − S dT, so (∂G/∂P)_T = V and (∂G/∂T)_P = −S.

questions.q: State the van't Hoff equation and interpret the sign for an endothermic reaction.
questions.m: d ln K/dT = ΔH°/(RT²) (or d ln K/d(1/T) = −ΔH°/R). For ΔH° > 0, ln K increases with T, so K grows and the equilibrium shifts toward products when temperature is raised; for exothermic reactions K decreases.

A rate constant doubles between 300 K and 310 K. The activation energy is approximately:
In the Lindemann–Hinshelwood mechanism, why does a unimolecular reaction change from second-order to first-order kinetics as pressure increases?
questions.m: A + M ⇌ A* + M (activation/deactivation), A* → P. With steady state on A*, rate = k₁k₂[A][M]/(k₋₁[M] + k₂). At low pressure k₋₁[M] ≪ k₂ and rate ≈ k₁[A][M] (second order: activation rate-limiting). At high pressure k₋₁[M] ≫ k₂ and rate ≈ (k₁k₂/k₋₁)[A] (first order: A* is in pre-equilibrium).

questions.q: For two nondegenerate levels separated by ΔE, the population ratio N₂/N₁ at temperature T is:
As T → 0 the molecular partition function q approaches:
c: The degeneracy of the ground state
questions.e: Only the lowest level is populated, so q → g₀ (taking its energy as zero).

questions.q: Using equipartition, what is C_V,m for a nonlinear polyatomic ideal gas considering only translation and rotation?
questions.m: Translation contributes (3/2)R, and rotation of a nonlinear molecule contributes another (3/2)R (three quadratic rotational terms, each ½R). C_V,m = 3R. Vibrations add more at higher temperature.

questions.q: A molecule shows a pure rotational microwave spectrum only if it:
c: Has a permanent electric dipole moment
Has an odd number of atoms
questions.e: Gross selection rule: permanent dipole; specific rule for a rigid rotor is ΔJ = ±1.

questions.q: In the harmonic-oscillator model, the zero-point vibrational energy is:
Which molecule has no IR-active stretching vibration?
questions.e: IR absorption requires a changing dipole; the stretch of a homonuclear diatomic produces none.
